title: IMU University Global Leadership Scholarship
program_type: University institutional tuition-fee reduction (partial tuition waiver) awarded to international students on admission to a listed undergraduate programme
administering_authority: IMU University (International Medical University, IMU Education Sdn Bhd)
implementing_agency: IMU Marketing and Enrolment Office / Admissions, IMU University
programme_action: IMU University Global Leadership Scholarship (GLS) 2026 intakes — institutional tuition-fee reduction for selected undergraduate programmes, open to both Malaysian and international students
description: IMU University states that the Global Leadership Scholarship (GLS) is open to both Malaysian and international students for selected programmes and intakes, with the scholarship amount of up to 25% reduction of tuition fees. The official Global Leadership Scholarships brochure published by the IMU Marketing and Enrolment Office (bullet file dated 2026/Jun/10/v4) lists ten undergraduate programmes, each with its own benefit and its own international tuition fee base: Digital Health up to 40%; Business Administration and Business Administration with Healthcare Management up to 35%; Bioveterinary Science, Nutrition and (as an Inaugural Intake Bursary) Cosmetic Science and Business Analytics RM30,000; Food Science Innovation RM25,000 as an Inaugural Intake Bursary; and Chiropractic RM10,000. The brochure is headed 'Guaranteed Global Leadership Scholarships' with 'Limited Places! Don't miss it!' and notes '* Terms and conditions apply'; it states every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy of the information but that it is subject to alteration without notice. IMU separately states that 'Scholarships are granted at the discretion of the University, and its decisions are final.' The award reduces tuition fees only: no living allowance, travel allowance, accommodation allowance, insurance or research allowance is published for it. IMU publishes no separate GLS application form; a programme page states that 'Students enrolling in the Business Administration programme at IMU for the 2026 intakes are eligible for the Global Leadership Scholarship, which offers up to 35% reduction in tuition fees' and that 'The scholarship amount will be evenly deducted every semester', so eligibility attaches to enrolment in a listed programme and intake through the ordinary undergraduate application. IMU accepts applications at any time, though it advises applying early due to high demand for these programmes and if an applicant needs to meet scholarship deadlines. The tuition costs from which the GLS is deducted, for international students, are published per programme in the same brochure, along with an Application Fee RM500 (non-refundable), Registration Fee RM2,500 (non-refundable), International Student Admin Fee RM2,500 (non-refundable), a Refundable Caution Deposit of RM1,000 and a payable-on-admission 50% refundable deposit for Ceramics or other programmes.

award_types: IMU Global Leadership Scholarship (GLS) — programme-specific tuition-fee reduction
programme_structure.award_types_detail: The GLS is a single scheme whose benefit is set per programme and per intake. The official Global Leadership Scholarships brochure for the 2026 intakes lists: Bioveterinary Science RM30,000*; Business Administration up to 35%*; Business Administration with Healthcare Management up to 35%*; Business Analytics RM30,000* (Inaugural Intake Bursary); Digital Health up to 40%*; Chiropractic RM10,000*; Cosmetic Science RM30,000* (Inaugural Intake Bursary); Food Science Innovation RM25,000* (Inaugural Intake Bursary); Nursing RM10,000*; Nutrition RM30,000*. IMU's Scholarships and Bursary web page states the broader scheme is 'up to 25% reduction of tuition fees' and applies the GLS to additional programmes not carried on the June 2026 brochure (Food Science Innovation RM15,000 GLS plus an additional RM10,000 for September joiners, Digital Health 20% for the 2026 intakes, Business Administration 25%, Business Administration with Healthcare Management 25%, Nursing RM10,000). Business Administration, Digital Health and Business Analytics additionally carry programme-level named scholarships that are separate schemes: the SKSEA BBA Scholarships (RM1,000 per IMU long semester, three long semesters maximum, for BBA students), the SKSEA Digital Health Scholarships, and the Yayasan Hasanah Business Analytics Scholarship for students with household income above RM5,000. IMU's own Financial Assistance Brochure records the GLS as continuing after charities and government loans in the order of funding application.
programme_structure.intake: February, April, July and September 2026 intakes, per programme: February/April/July/Sep for Business Administration, Business Administration with Healthcare Management and Digital Health; July/Sep for Bioveterinary Science and Cosmetic Science; September for Business Analytics, Food Science Innovation, Nursing and Nutrition; April/September for Chiropractic. The IMU academic calendar lists semester registration for the 2025/2026 session: Semester 3 from 17 November 2025 to 15 March 2026 (incl. final exam recess/submissions 8 April to 15 March and examinations 16 March to 21 March 2026), Semester 1 from 12 January 2026 to 9 May 2026 (incl. final exam recess/submissions 6 April to 3 May 2026 and examinations 4 May to 9 May 2026), Semester 2 from 4 May 2026 to 8 August 2026 (incl. final exam recess/submissions 29 June to 26 July 2026 and examinations 27 July to 8 August 2026), Semester 3 from 22 June 2026 to 3 October 2026 (incl. final exam recess/submissions 24 August to 20 September 2026 and examinations 21 September to 3 October 2026) and a short semester from 12 May 2025 to 30 January 2026. The brochure itself is headed '2026 Intakes'.
programme_structure.quota: Not published as a number. The brochure reads 'Limited Places! Don't miss it!' and in large display 'Up To' alongside the percentage benefits, indicating the reduction is capped and competitive.
programme_structure.allocation: Selected IMU University undergraduate programmes only.
programme_structure.award_categories: Programme-specific tuition-fee reductions and inaugural-intake bursaries

duration: 3-5 years full-time national undergraduate programmes, by programme

funding.scholarship_type: Institutional partial tuition-fee reduction (tuition waiver). Not a full scholarship and not a living allowance.
funding.monthly_amount_note: IMU publishes no monthly stipend, living allowance or maintenance payment for the Global Leadership Scholarship on any official imu.edu.my page reachable on 2026-10-03. All benefit fields other than tuition are recorded as null.
funding.travel_amount_note: IMU publishes no travel, flight or relocation allowance for the Global Leadership Scholarship.
funding.fully_funded_note: The GLS is a partial tuition-fee reduction only. It is not fully funded: it provides no living allowance, no travel allowance, no accommodation, no insurance and no research or book allowance, and for most programmes it does not cover the whole tuition fee (the benefits run from RM10,000 to RM30,000 or from 20% to 40% of tuition, against international tuition fees of RM92,000 to RM363,600). No scholarship service bond or repayment obligation is published for the GLS, but separately IMU requires all international students to pay a refundable Personal Bond to the Malaysian Immigration Department based on country of origin when they register.
funding.funding_amount_note: RM30,000 is the highest stated absolute award published in the official brochure (Bioveterinary Science; Nutrition; Cosmetic Science and Business Analytics as Inaugural Intake Bursaries). The other benefits are stated as percentages 'up to' 40% (Digital Health), up to 35% (Business Administration and Business Administration with Healthcare Management), RM25,000 (Food Science Innovation) or RM10,000 (Chiropractic, Nursing), so RM30,000 is a ceiling for the absolute-value awards only and must not be presented as the award every student receives.
funding.funding_period_note: The benefit is applied as a tuition-fee reduction spread across the programme. IMU states for Business Administration: 'The scholarship amount will be evenly deducted every semester.'

coverage: Tuition-fee reduction on ten listed IMU University undergraduate programmes for the 2026 intakes: Bioveterinary Science RM30,000; Business Administration up to 35%; Business Administration with Healthcare Management up to 35%; Business Analytics RM30,000 (Inaugural Intake Bursary); Digital Health up to 40%; Chiropractic RM10,000; Cosmetic Science RM30,000 (Inaugural Intake Bursary); Food Science Innovation RM25,000 (Inaugural Intake Bursary); Nursing RM10,000; Nutrition RM30,000
The reduction is applied by IMU: 'The scholarship amount will be evenly deducted every semester'
IMU's Scholarships and Bursary page states the wider scheme is 'up to 25% reduction of tuition fees' and describes the GLS as a reduction of tuition fees
No living allowance, travel allowance, accommodation allowance, insurance, research, book, equipment or family allowance is published for the GLS
coverage_limitations: The GLS is a partial tuition reduction. The absolute awards (RM10,000 to RM30,000) do not cover the full international tuition fee for any programme: the lowest international fee base is Nursing at RM104,000 and the highest is Chiropractic at RM363,600.

The percentage benefits are published as 'up to' figures (up to 40%, up to 35%), so the actual reduction for a given student is at the University's discretion and cannot be predicted from the published brochure.

The GLS is restricted to the ten listed programmes. It is not published for other IMU undergraduate programmes such as Medicine, Dentistry, Pharmacy, Chinese Medicine, Psychology or Pharmaceutical Chemistry.
The brochure does not state which semesters the deduction covers or whether it continues across the full programme, other than that the amount will be evenly deducted every semester.
IMU publishes no GLS-specific minimum grade, CGPA, English score or country-of-origin criterion, no GLS-specific document list and no GLS-specific selection weighting.

The brochure itself states 'Every effort has been made to ensure the accuracy of the information given in this brochure but it is subject to alteration without notice', so the amounts and fee bases can change without notice.

IMU's separate Scholarships and Bursary page states different figures for some programmes (Digital Health 20%, Business Administration 25%, Business Administration with Healthcare Management 25%, Food Science Innovation RM15,000 plus RM10,000 for September joiners) than the June 2026 brochure; both are official imu.edu.my pages but the brochure is the more specific and more recent document.

International students must separately meet IMU's requirement of a valid full-time student pass from the Malaysian Immigration Department before registration, and pay a refundable Personal Bond to the Immigration Department set by country of origin; neither is part of the GLS award.
final_year_condition: Not published in the GLS brochure. IMU's general undergraduate admission route requires completion of a recognised pre-university qualification before entry; IMU publishes country-by-country undergraduate entry requirements on its international admissions pages and its Applying To IMU page states that the equivalence of the qualification is assessed by IMU together with the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA).
equivalent_degree_note: IMU recognises a wide range of qualifications for entry to its undergraduate programmes and states that applicants whose qualification is not listed should contact IMU for an assessment; equivalence is determined by IMU together with the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA). No list of accepted equivalent qualifications is published on the imu.edu.my pages reachable on 2026-10-03, so none is reproduced here.
previous_award_restriction: Not published for the GLS. IMU's general guidance in the Financial Assistance Brochure places the GLS in the order of funding application after charities and government loans, and IMU's Aspire scholarship page states that applicants of Aspire are not allowed to hold any other scholarships or sponsorships, but no equivalent concurrent-funding rule is published for the GLS.

eligibility.citizenship: No nationality restriction. IMU's Scholarships and Bursary page states the scholarship is 'open to both Malaysian and International students for selected programmes and intakes', and the brochure itself lists both Malaysian and International tuition fee bases for every programme. This is the key distinction from IMU's other schemes: IMU-Merit and IMU-Need are restricted to Malaysian citizens, and the SKSEA Digital Health Scholarships, Times Foundation Science Scholarships and several others are likewise restricted to Malaysian students.
eligibility.residence_requirement: No residence requirement published. International students must hold a valid full-time student pass from the Malaysian Immigration Department before they can register at IMU.
eligibility.secondary_school_requirement: Not published for the GLS specifically. Admission to IMU undergraduate programmes generally requires a recognised pre-university qualification, whose equivalence is assessed by IMU together with the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA).
eligibility.academic_requirements: No GLS-specific minimum grade or CGPA is published. General undergraduate entry to the GLS programmes is assessed on the pre-university qualification held; the brochure lists the award per programme but sets no academic threshold for receiving it.
eligibility.language_requirement: Not published for the GLS specifically. Admission requirements for individual GLS programmes are published on the programme pages: for example Business Administration lists IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 46, CAE 160, CPE 160, Cambridge Linguaskill 160, PTE 51, MUET Band 3 and the application fee route, with exemptions noted. IMU states it recognises a wide range of qualifications and that applicants whose qualification is not listed should contact IMU for an assessment. The 2025/2026 IMU University Open Day Programme Booklet also lists programme-level English pre-approved status conditions (for nursing: 20% English pre-approved status score; for the Bachelor of Science [Ton] in Business Analytics 2026 intakes: 20% and for Digital Health 2026 intakes: 20%), which are programme admission conditions rather than GLS conditions.
eligibility.leadership_requirement: Not published. The scheme's name refers to global leadership, but no leadership, community-service or extracurricular criterion is published for the GLS.
eligibility.financial_need: Not published. The GLS is not described as need-based and no income or B40 criterion is published for it. Note that other IMU schemes are explicitly need-based (for example the Aspire scholarship is open to students from families with household income below RM5,000.00 per month), so applicants should not assume the GLS is needs-tested.
eligibility.enrolment_status_requirement: The scholarship applies to students enrolling at IMU for the 2026 intakes in a listed programme. IMU's programme page states 'Students enrolling in the Business Administration programme at IMU for the 2026 intakes are eligible for the Global Leadership Scholarship'.
eligibility.health_requirement: Not published for the GLS. IMU's programme brochure requirement states that international students should complete the Health Declaration Form as part of the application, and its programme pages note that applicants must satisfy health and visa requirements.
eligibility.field_restrictions: Restricted to the ten programmes listed in the brochure. The per-programme benefits differ, so an applicant's outcome depends entirely on which listed programme they enrol in.

academic_requirements.percentage_note: IMU publishes no minimum percentage, CGPA or grade threshold for the Global Leadership Scholarship. The brochure states the benefit per programme but attaches no academic condition to it. application_method.application_route: Apply for admission to one of the ten listed IMU University undergraduate programmes through IMU's Online Admissions Application. There is NO separate Global Leadership Scholarship application form, portal or essay: IMU's programme page states 'Students enrolling in the Business Administration programme at IMU for the 2026 intakes are eligible for the Global Leadership Scholarship', so the award is considered automatically on admission and enrolment. IMU states 'Applications can be made at any time, however it is advantageous for you to apply early due to high demand for these programmes or if you need to meet scholarship deadlines.'
application_steps: Choose one of the ten GLS programmes and confirm the intake month listed for it in the brochure (February, April, July or September 2026, depending on programme).
Create an account and apply for admission through IMU's Online Admissions Application at https://imu.edu.my/online-admissions-application/.

Upload the Application Documents to progress to the next step of IMU's online application form: identity document (Malaysian IC / Passport number), health declaration form, another identity document, academic transcript, academic certificate, English proficiency certificate, referee report and evidence of extracurricular participation. IMU states that undergraduate applicants must upload transcripts and documents as required and that international students are required to accept an offer by the published offer expiry date.
Obtain an Offer of Acceptance from IMU for the chosen programme and the intended intake.
Enrol for the listed intake. IMU states that scholarships are granted at the discretion of the University and that its decisions are final.
IMU applies the award as a tuition reduction: 'The scholarship amount will be evenly deducted every semester.'

The published international fee bases for the 2026 intakes are RM104,000 (Nursing), RM130,500 (Business Administration, Business Administration with Healthcare Management, Business Analytics, Digital Health), RM145,200 (Cosmetic Science, Food Science Innovation, Nutrition), RM229,500 (Bioveterinary Science) and RM363,600 (Chiropractic). The GLS reduces these by the programme-specific amount. IMU also publishes, for its programmes, an Application Fee RM500 (non-refundable), a Registration Fee RM2,500 (non-refundable), an International Student Admin Fee RM2,500 (non-refundable) and a Refundable Caution Deposit of RM1,000.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.student_agreement: No GLS-specific student agreement is published. IMU's programme brochure states that students must sign and abide by the IMU Student Handbook, Student Code of Conduct, Professional Indemnity Insurance Policy, Personal Data Protection Notice and the terms and conditions stated in their offer letter/accepted offer. IMU states that scholarships are granted at the University's discretion and that its decisions are final, and the brochure notes '* Terms and conditions apply' without publishing them.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.common_services: IMU publishes an e-community service, counselling programme, welfare fund, medical diagnosis and outpatient or inpatient medical treatment, e-learning resources, and off-campus housing guidance.
student_rights_and_cost_protection.bond_requirement: No scholarship service bond is published for the GLS. Separately, international students must pay a refundable Personal Bond to the Malaysian Immigration Department, set by country of origin, in order to register; this is an immigration requirement, not a scholarship obligation.

application_readiness_checklist: Confirm which of the ten GLS programmes you are applying to and check its exact intake months and RM figure in the official Global Leadership Scholarships brochure, because the benefit differs by programme.
Check whether the intake you want is still open. As of 2026-10-03 the February, April, July and September 2026 intakes have passed, so target the next intake.

Contact IMU before relying on any figure. IMU accepts applications at any time and states you should apply early if you need to meet scholarship deadlines, but publishes no GLS closing date, so confirm the current cycle by writing to IMU.

Prepare the eight Application Documents that IMU's online application requires: identity document (IC or Passport number), Health Declaration Form, another identity document, academic transcript, academic certificate, English proficiency certificate, referee report and evidence of extracurricular participation.
Keep each attachment under 3MB, as IMU states attachments are limited to 3MB each.

Prepare English evidence against the published Business Administration admission requirement (IELTS 5.5, TOEFL iBT 46, CAE 160, CPE 160, Cambridge Linguaskill 160, PTE 51, MUET Band 3) as a proxy for what IMU expects, and contact IMU if your qualification is not listed.

Budget for the full international tuition fee in case the reduction is not granted or is lower than the brochure figure: RM104,000 to RM363,600 by programme, plus the RM500 application fee, RM2,500 registration fee, RM2,500 International Student Admin Fee, RM1,000 refundable caution deposit and the Immigration-set Personal Bond.
Register with IMU for the accepted intake and await the award decision, which is taken at the University's discretion.

practical_application_data.motivation_letter_strategy: No essay, motivation letter or personal statement is published for the Global Leadership Scholarship, so none is required for the award itself. IMU's online application does request a Referee Report and evidence of extracurricular participation, so those are the only narrative or reference materials to prepare. If IMU requests narrative input, keep it factual: the listed programme and intake applied for, the qualification held and its equivalence, the English evidence held, and the funding plan for the balance of the international tuition fee.
profile_fit_labels: Applicant enrolling in one of the ten GLS programmes (Business Administration, Business Administration with Healthcare Management, Business Analytics, Digital Health, Cosmetic Science, Food Science Innovation, Bioveterinary Science, Chiropractic, Nursing, Nutrition)
Applicant who can fund the balance of the international tuition fee, which is RM104,000 to RM363,600 by programme
Applicant willing to accept a discretionary reduction of 'up to' figures rather than a guaranteed amount
common_mistakes: Assuming the headline 'up to 25% reduction of tuition fees' is the amount. The official brochure sets a different benefit per programme, including up to 40% for Digital Health and up to 35% for the two Business Administration programmes.
Assuming an 'up to 35%' or 'up to 40%' figure is guaranteed. The brochure says 'up to' and IMU states the scholarships are granted at the University's discretion and its decisions are final.
Budgeting as though the GLS is a full scholarship. It is tuition reduction only: no living allowance, travel, accommodation, insurance or book allowance is published for it.
Applying to a programme that is not one of the ten listed programmes and expecting the award.
Looking for a separate GLS application form. There is none: eligibility attaches to enrolment in a listed programme and intake.

Applying for a non-listed IMU scheme assuming it is open to international students. IMU-Merit and IMU-Need are restricted to Malaysian citizens, as are the SKSEA Digital Health Scholarships, the Times Foundation Science Scholarships and several others.

Confusing the GLS with IMU's Aspire scholarship, which is a different scheme with its own route (register and apply via start.imu.edu.my/scholarships/aspire/) and a household-income condition below RM5,000.00 per month.
Forgetting the non-refundable RM2,500 International Student Admin Fee and the Immigration-set Personal Bond when budgeting for international study.
Assuming the June 2026 brochure figures still apply to a later intake. IMU states the brochure is subject to alteration without notice.

risk_flags.risk: The GLS benefit is programme-specific and its percentage awards are published only as 'up to' figures.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant cannot predict the actual reduction from the brochure, so a budget built on 'up to 40%' may be materially wrong.
risk_flags.mitigation: Read the exact line for your programme in the official brochure, contact IMU to ask whether the figure applies to your intake and circumstances, and budget for the full international tuition fee of RM104,000-RM363,600 in the meantime.

risk_flags.risk: The 2026 intakes shown in the brochure have passed as of 2026-10-03.
risk_flags.impact: Any figure quoted now is historical; the next intake's benefit and fee base may differ.
risk_flags.mitigation: IMU states the brochure is subject to alteration without notice and to visit www.imu.edu.my for the most up-to-date information. Confirm the next cycle with IMU before relying on any amount.

risk_flags.risk: Two official IMU pages publish different figures for the same programme (the Scholarships and Bursary page shows Digital Health 20%, Business Administration 25%, Business Administration with Healthcare Management 25% and Food Science Innovation RM15,000 plus RM10,000 for September joiners, while the June 2026 brochure shows Digital Health up to 40%, both Business Administration programmes up to 35%, and Food Science Innovation RM25,000).
risk_flags.impact: An applicant reading the wrong page will budget against the wrong benefit.
risk_flags.mitigation: The dedicated Global Leadership Scholarships brochure is the more specific and more recent document (dated 2026/Jun/10/v4) and is used as the primary source in this record. Confirm with IMU which figures apply.

risk_flags.risk: No GLS-specific academic threshold, English score, document list or selection weighting is published.
risk_flags.impact: An applicant cannot determine whether they will receive the award or how their application will be judged.
risk_flags.mitigation: Treat the award as a discretionary tuition reduction attached to enrolment rather than a competitive scholarship, and prepare a funded plan that does not depend on it.

risk_flags.impact: An international student relying on the award to fund their studies would have no living allowance, travel, accommodation or insurance.
risk_flags.mitigation: Fund living costs separately. IMU publishes no GLS allowance; budget using off-campus housing guidance and the living cost of Kuala Lumpur.

risk_flags.risk: The scheme is easy to confuse with IMU-Merit and IMU-Need, which are Malaysian-citizen-only.
risk_flags.impact: An international applicant who finds IMU-Merit or IMU-Need may wrongly conclude IMU has no international scholarship, or apply to a scheme they cannot access.
risk_flags.mitigation: The GLS is the IMU scheme that IMU itself states is open to both Malaysian and international students. IMU-Merit and IMU-Need are explicitly restricted to Malaysian citizens and are excluded from this record.

database_notes: MALAYSIA-TARGET RESEARCH: The assignment targeted IMU University and Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman (UTAR) international undergraduate scholarship schemes.

UTAR EXCLUDED - NO INTERNATIONAL SCHOLARSHIP: Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman's Division of Industrial and Community Studies FAQ (diss.utar.edu.my/FAQ.php, an official utar.edu.my domain) states in the answer to 'How can international students apply for scholarship?' that 'UTAR provides no scholarship for international students.' The university's scholarship-bursa page and the industry-and-community listing also describe financial aid only for Malaysians or permanent residents and lists the IMU University YTAR co-award only as a partner scholarship of the Malaysian Tunku Abdul Rahman Scholarship. No UTAR scholarship for international undergraduates was recorded, because per RESEARCH_PROTOCOL.md no scholarship should be invented to fill a slot. Substitution: the IMU University Global Leadership Scholarship, which is the IMU scheme that IMU itself states is open to international students.

CHOICE OF AWARD: IMU-Merit and IMU-Need were excluded per the assignment because IMU's own official IMU-Merit scholarship brochure states that to be eligible for the IMU-Merit scholarship, an applicant must be a Malaysian citizen. Other IMU schemes verified as restricted to Malaysians are the SKSEA Digital Health Scholarships, the Times Foundation Science Scholarships (Malaysians only, for BSc (Hons) Mathematics and Statistics, BSc (Hons) Science (Biology), BSc (Hons) Science (Food Studies) and Foundation programmes), and several others. The GLS is the one IMU scheme IMU states is open to international students.

AMOUNT RECORDED: The absolute awards published in the official brochure run from RM10,000 (Chiropractic, Nursing) to RM30,000 (Bioveterinary Science, Nutrition, Cosmetic Science and Business Analytics Inaugural Intake Bursaries), plus RM25,000 for the Food Science Innovation Inaugural Intake Bursary. The percentage awards are published only as 'up to' 40% (Digital Health) and up to 35% (Business Administration, Business Administration with Healthcare Management). No additional absolute figure, for example Digital Health RM20,000 or Business Administration RM6,000, is published in the official Global Leadership Scholarships brochure, so none has been recorded.

FEE BASE: The international tuition fee bases recorded (RM104,000-RM363,600 by programme) are the fees the award is deducted from, taken from the same brochure, and are not an award value. IMU states the brochure is subject to alteration without notice and to visit www.imu.edu.my for the most up-to-date information.

APPLICATION FEE: An Application Fee of RM500 (non-refundable) is published in the brochure. IMU also publishes a Registration Fee RM2,500 (non-refundable), an International Student Admin Fee RM2,500 (non-refundable), a Refundable Caution Deposit of RM1,000, and a payable-on-admission 50% refundable deposit for Ceramics or other programmes, plus an annual student visa renewal fee. IMU's Applying To IMU page also states that applicants may be required to pay a registration fee or caution deposit.

NO SEPARATE SCHOLARSHIP APPLICATION: IMU's programme pages state that students enrolling in the listed programme for the 2026 intakes are eligible for the Global Leadership Scholarship and that the scholarship amount will be evenly deducted every semester. There is therefore no separate GLS form, portal, essay or interview, and eligibility attaches to enrolment. IMU states scholarships are granted at the University's discretion and its decisions are final.

NO PUBLISHED DEADLINE: IMU publishes no closing date, submission time or timezone for the GLS. deadline_date is recorded as null and deadline_precision as 'varies', per the schema rule that no exact calendar date may be guessed. The published timing is intake-based: the February, April, July and September 2026 intakes. The only exact dates IMU publishes in the surrounding pages are the IMU-Merit scholarship windows (application 10 July-7 August 2026 for the September intake, with a SPM year end 2025 result requirement), which belong to a different, Malaysian-only scheme and are recorded here only as context.

SOURCE CONFLICT: IMU's Scholarships and Bursary page states the GLS is 'up to 25% reduction of tuition fees' and applies a 20% figure to Digital Health and 25% to the two Business Administration programmes, whereas the June 2026 brochure gives up to 40% for Digital Health and up to 35% for the Business Administration programmes. Both are official imu.edu.my pages; this record follows the dedicated brochure because it is more specific, programme-by-programme and later-dated (v4, June 2026).

LOGO: The IMU University institutional logo was taken from IMU's own domain, https://imu.edu.my/, and confirmed by an HTTP HEAD request to return HTTP 200 with Content-Type image/png and a size of 5,563 bytes. Pixel analysis of the asset confirms it is a dark logo (average opaque RGB 37, 0, 136, mean luminance approximately 27), so it is not a white-on-transparent wordmark and is visible on a light card. IMU's schema.org Organization block on that page declares https://imu.edu.my/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/IMU_Logo_Icon.png as its logo; that asset also returns HTTP 200, image/png, 15,004 bytes, but is a palette-mode 1001x1001 icon tile with mean luminance approximately 4, i.e. effectively a dark solid block that would render as a filled square on a light card, so the horizontal header wordmark was preferred. No third-party or aggregator source was used and no other domain was probed.

ENGLISH REQUIREMENT: The English figures recorded are the published Business Administration admission requirements, which is the deepest-verified GLS programme page on imu.edu.my. IMU publishes no English requirement specific to the GLS, so these are admission requirements, not a scholarship threshold.

COMPLETENESS: The record is complete on every required key. Substantive fields that IMU does not publish for the GLS, for example monthly_stipend, travel allowance, insurance, bond, selection criteria and weighting, are deliberately null or 'not published' rather than filled with plausible figures, so _completeness_score reflects verified-but-thin data on undisclosed benefit instruments rather than missing keys.

STATUS: status is CLOSED because IMU's official brochure is headed 2026 Intakes and the February, April, July and September 2026 intakes have all passed as of 2026-10-03. IMU nevertheless states applications can be made at any time and that applicants should apply early if they need to meet scholarship deadlines, so the next cycle is the 2027 intakes. A next-cycle verification is recommended in February 2027.

CURRENCY: All monetary figures are Malaysian Ringgit (MYR), abbreviated RM in IMU's pages. IMU's brochure publishes Malaysian and international fee bases side by side; the international bases are the ones relevant to this record.

unverified_or_removed_claims: No GLS-specific application deadline exists on any official imu.edu.my page reachable on 2026-10-03, so deadline_date is null and deadline_precision is 'varies'. No date has been inferred from the intake months.

No GLS-specific academic threshold, English score, selection criterion or weighting is published. The English figures recorded are the published Business Administration admission requirements and are labelled as admission requirements, not scholarship thresholds.
No GLS-specific document list exists. The documents recorded are the eight Application Documents that IMU's online application requires of every applicant.
No quota or number of award places is published for the GLS or for any single programme; the brochure's 'Limited Places!' is the only published signal.

The brochure's '* Terms and conditions apply' footnote is not followed by any published terms, so renewal, maintenance and repayment conditions cannot be recorded. IMU-Merit's published terms (maintenance of CGPA 3.30 per semester for up to 4 semesters; repayment on withdrawal) belong to a different, Malaysian-citizen-only scheme and have NOT been attributed to the GLS.

No living allowance, travel allowance, accommodation allowance, insurance, research, book, equipment or family allowance is published for the GLS, so those fields are null or 'not published' rather than filled.

No total award value is computed. The award is programme-specific (RM10,000 to RM30,000, or 20% to 40% of programme-specific tuition) and the brochure states the percentages are 'up to', so a single total would be fabrication.

The fee figures of RM130,500 (Business Administration) and RM229,500 / RM363,600 / RM145,200 / RM104,000 are the international fee bases from which the award is deducted, not an award value. Business Administration is also published on IMU's programme page as 5 long semesters of RM21,200 each plus 1 short semester at RM12,250 and an Industrial Training at RM12,250.

The 50% refundable deposit payable on admission and the RM2,500 monthly cost line in IMU's programme brochure are published for the Dentistry Foundation in Dentistry [Source] programme rather than for the ten GLS programmes, so they are not recorded as GLS-specific costs.

IMU's Scholarships and Bursary web page states Digital Health 20%, Business Administration 25%, Business Administration with Healthcare Management 25% and Food Science Innovation RM15,000 plus RM10,000 for September joiners, which conflicts with the June 2026 brochure's up to 40%, up to 35%, up to 35% and RM25,000. The brochure is followed as the primary source; the conflict is disclosed rather than resolved by assumption.

IMU's own 2025/2026 IMU University Open Day Programme Booklet lists a Medical Biotechnology Global Leadership Scholarship of RM10,000 (inaugural intake) under Medical Biotechnology, which is NOT one of the ten programmes in the June 2026 brochure, so it has not been recorded in this GLS entry and is flagged for confirmation.

No UTAR scholarship for international undergraduates exists to record: Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman's Division of Industrial and Community Studies FAQ states 'UTAR provides no scholarship for international students'. Per the research protocol no scholarship was invented for UTAR.

The IMU University YTAR partner scholarship shown in the Tunku Abdul Rahman Foundation's programme pages is a partner scholarship of the Malaysian Tunku Abdul Rahman Scholarship and is open to Malaysian citizens only, so it is excluded from this record.

Attempts to read the Nutrition Programme Brochure page directly returned no extractable text, and the www2.utar.edu.my/contentlisting.jsp page returned a 404, so no additional detail was drawn from either.

IMU's brochure states that all information is subject to alteration without notice, so every figure in this record is dated to 2026-06-10 (the brochure's own file date) and must be re-verified for the next intake cycle.
